comment.body:
I am not convinced `AbcvlibActivity` should own publisher-specific startup orchestration.

Before this PR, the base activity was mostly a bare app skeleton for USB/output/main-loop setup, and apps opted into publishers themselves. This PR adds publisher imports, publisher startup completion state, `startPublishersWithFailureHandling`, retry wiring, and publisher-specific dialog handling to the base activity.

Apps may or may not use publishers, so this makes every `AbcvlibActivity` subclass inherit publisher-specific API/behavior even when it is not needed. If `PublisherStartupFailureDialog` is intended to be the reusable UI boundary for publisher failures, why does `AbcvlibActivity` also need publisher-specific startup orchestration?

Could this be moved back toward the publisher layer, with `AbcvlibActivity` only exposing generic app-shell hooks where needed, such as delaying/releasing the main loop? Apps that use publishers could wire `PublisherManager` into those hooks explicitly.
